title: Existence of normalized constant left-module comparisons
statement: Given a normalized exact lift d over small sites J,K and an arbitrary ring Λ, normalized module isomorphisms exist for composition and a specified isomorphism of set inverse images. For each object X of the source site, restriction to J.over X admits a geometric adjunction and a lift identified sectionwise with module restriction followed by restriction of scalars along the constant-ring localization isomorphism. No uniqueness is assumed here; the parent proves uniqueness by faithful forgetting and cancellation. The underlying notions are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: Apply AddCommGrpCat.leftExactFunctorForgetEquivalence sectionwise to lift a natural transformation between the underlying sets of finite-limit-preserving module functors to an abelian transformation. If it commutes with each constant scalar endomorphism, restrictHomEquivOfIsLocallySurjective for toSheafify extends the map uniquely to a module morphism. Faithful forgetting proves naturality; reflection of isomorphisms lifts a set natural isomorphism.

For a presentation comparison, conjugate the specified set natural isomorphism by the two moduleSetIso comparisons. Naturality and scalar_compatibility show that this transformation commutes with constant scalar endomorphisms, so the preceding lifting construction gives the required normalized module isomorphism. For composition use the composite of the two moduleSetIso comparisons and apply scalar_compatibility twice. The stated normalization equations follow by cancellation.

For the over-site, use Mathlib overPullback, sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous and its finite-limit preservation, and apply constantLeftModuleTransport. Use pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility for the over-forgetful functor to identify the restricted constant ring with the constant ring on the over-site; the toSheafify compatibility equation proves its normalization on scalars. Sectionwise module restriction followed by restrictScalars along the inverse ring comparison has the same underlying set functor and constant scalar maps. It preserves finite limits by reflection through forgetting. Lift the normalized set comparison by the preceding construction, obtaining the claimed module isomorphism and section equation.
